<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written and conceded the right things (PRO conceded growth matters; CON conceded flourishing is the end). The decisive clash was enforceability. CON's reframe — a headline target is a leash, not a values statement — created a burden PRO never fully discharged: name the number that can be missed. PRO's answer ("there is no single figure; 'primary' means governing priority") is a defensible reading of the motion, but CON immediately converted it into the fork it had set up in [B2.2]: aggregate and the government controls the weights; refuse to aggregate and you have the dashboard CON already conceded. PRO's admission that the legislature fixes the domains handed CON its cleanest hit ("the body being judged writes the terms of its own examination"), and PRO's reply — outsiders can expose it, GDP can also be cherry-picked — parried without neutralizing, since GDP's rules genuinely cannot be rewritten by the chancellor. PRO's strongest live route, the disputed case of output rising while health and security fall, survived partially: CON's answer (GDP's narrowness is its discipline; specific biting instruments police health) is a good reframe, but it does rely on a suite of indicators, which PRO could have pressed as structurally identical to its own framework with output merely privileged. PRO gestured at this in closing ("the narrower the claim, the weaker its entitlement") but never sharpened it into a symmetry-breaking attack. CON also kept the political-economy point live — targets operate through fear, and stagnation becomes "nuance" under a broad headline — which PRO answered mostly by logic rather than incentive. Execution costs: CON was clipped twice, losing the end of two arguments; PRO stayed within limits. Both handled Pressure Questions properly with A1:/A2: labels. On balance CON made the choice easier to decide and left the harder unanswered question on PRO's side.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's "Name the number" question and its follow-up in Rebuttal 2: PRO's answer that "there is no single figure, and the motion does not require one" was turned into the fork that a non-aggregated framework is just the dashboard CON already conceded, compounded by PRO's admission that the legislature — the governing majority — fixes the domains.</best_rebuttal>
